note: Stories cluster the last 24 hours of collector items. Summaries come only from item titles and feed summaries; open the links before citing details.

stories.headline: Turkish parliament begins ratifying Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
stories.summary: Parliament approved the first article of the bill ratifying the Mecca defence pact among Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. The pact contains a collective defence clause, and ratification comes while Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continue.
stories.turkey: Ratification ties Türkiye into a collective defence commitment with Riyadh and Islamabad during an active Gulf conflict.

stories.headline: IRGC says mines destroyed four tankers in Hormuz and two vessels were seized
stories.summary: The IRGC says four oil tankers that entered a prohibited passage south of the Strait of Hormuz were destroyed by naval mines. It also says two other vessels were seized or halted. Gulf News reports the four tankers caught fire, and Trump said US forces are 'locked and loaded'.
stories.turkey: Escalation at Hormuz threatens energy supply and prices on which Türkiye depends.

stories.headline: Vance and Trump blame Iran war for Republican midterm losses
stories.summary: Vice President Vance said the Iran war, cost of living and US-Israel ties drove voters to the Democrats. Trump called it 'largely true' that the war caused the losses, but said he 'had to do it' and would make the same decision again.
stories.turkey: Washington's political cost from the Iran war shapes how likely a US exit or escalation is on Türkiye's border.

stories.headline: Democrats take Congress and weigh war-powers limits on Trump's Iran war
stories.summary: Democrats won majorities in both chambers, with Senate control confirmed at 51 seats and Jeffries set to become House speaker. Leaders including Schumer vow to end the Iran war and are weighing war-powers and funding levers, though analysts note they lack veto-override numbers. The incoming Congress will also scrutinise the $1.5 trillion Pentagon budget and the roughly $90 billion Iran war request.
stories.turkey: A Democratic Congress changes the terms of US policy toward Türkiye as well as Iran and Israel.

stories.headline: Trump says no immediate Iran strike plan, but Washington is split on escalation
stories.summary: Trump said there is no immediate plan to strike Iran, though US forces are 'locked and loaded'. He warned of a 'heavy hit' and said he can end the operation when he chooses. Reports describe disagreement among officials over escalation versus a negotiated exit, and analysts say the midterm result leaves him with few good options.
stories.turkey: Whether the US escalates or negotiates an exit decides how much regional spillover Türkiye faces.

stories.summary: Iran's Supreme Leader said US hostility will continue whichever party controls Congress. He laid out a doctrine of immediate responses with no geographic limit to any renewed attack. He cited Hormuz management and strikes on US bases as a response that could widen.

stories.headline: Iranian officials threaten retaliation, including on European bases, if attacked
stories.summary: IRGC and government figures warned that Iran would drop proportional retaliation and target enemy leaders and assets if attacked. An Iranian MP told Euronews that bases in Italy and Germany would be fired on if used by the US. Berlin says it is working with regional states to prevent renewed attacks, and Iran rebuked the German foreign minister.

Journalists including Ağırel and Saymaz have been indicted over fund coverage, and AKP-MHP lawmakers rejected another inquiry bid. The FT calls the $20 billion crisis a Ponzi-to-Ponzi scheme affecting over 455,000 investors.

stories.headline: Israel certifies election results; Herzog opens coalition talks
stories.summary: The election commission confirmed final results that cost Netanyahu's coalition its majority and found no fraud. Herzog began consultations, with Eisenkot leading endorsements, including from Raam, while the Religious Zionists and Shas back Netanyahu. Shas lost nearly half its seats and Deri asked to step down. A government must be formed within 13 weeks or early elections follow.
